# fiber

> **v0 alpha, pre-1.0, not recommended for production.** Interfaces are still moving and may change between minor versions. fiber is a library, not a service: no binary, nothing listens. The in-memory composition is complete and tested; the Redis and Postgres bus backends and the Postgres store backends pass the same conformance suites as Memory when a Redis or Postgres is supplied (CI's integration job).

> Agent platform and low-latency pub/sub bus for agents. Define an agent with a declarative spec, tag it from Slack, GitHub, Jira or a schedule, and stream its events to any subscriber while delivering them to any destination. The design turns on one idea: where a tag is raised and where its answer lands are independent, which is what makes it a mesh rather than a set of integrations. Composes three libraries: saige (agent loop, typed deltas, RAG citations), anchor (durable execution, ledger as truth, replay), and playscape (sandboxed execution nodes, NGAC access control). Go module `github.com/urmzd/fiber`; the root package `fiber` is the composition root a program composes in Go (`fiber.New(ctx, ...Option)`; no binary, no config files, no env vars), and warp is the platform built on it.

## Key Concepts

- Topic: one namespace, matched by segment-wise prefix. `agent` (every agent), `agent:<name>` (every run of one agent, what users listen to), `agent:<name>:<runID>` (one run, where events are published). No wildcard language. `agent:docs` does NOT cover `agent:docs-bot`.
- Not topics, deliberately: event kind and agent revision are FIELDS filtered on one subscription (`envelope.Filter`); tenant is an authorization scope taken from the caller's credential and never named by a subscriber; destination is a `Route` on the run.
- Connector faces, independent and derived by `connector.RolesOf` rather than declared: `Trigger` raises tags, `Sink` renders events onto a native surface, `Actor` contributes native verbs as agent tools. slack/github/jira do all three; cron triggers only (a schedule has no surface); webhook sinks only (an outbound POST raises nothing).
- N:M delivery: one tag fans out to many sinks, one sink serves many agents, and each `Route` selects its own kinds via `Route.Wants`. A GitHub comment takes every delta and is edited in place while a webhook on the same run takes only `lifecycle.completed`.
- Revision pinning: an `AgentSpec` is immutable; revising appends N+1. A run pins its revision (and its content hash) at accept time and executes against it forever, because anchor replays workflows from the top and an unpinned run would diverge with `ErrNonDeterministic`. Delete is a tombstone: `Get(name, rev)` still resolves so a completed run stays explicable.
- Dual publish: `anchor.Emit` writes the durable per-run journal (replay, cursor resume); `bus.Publish` writes the live cross-run bus (observers, delivery). The journal is truth, the bus is flow.
- Idempotency: `Tag.ID` is the run id, so a Slack retry or GitHub redelivery joins the existing run instead of answering twice.
- Stop: `runtime.Stop` (or `App.Stop`) records the request on the run in the anchor ledger (`runtime.WithStopLedger`), then publishes `control.stop` to the caller's tenant-keyed `agent:_control:stop-<key>` as the fast path. Each attempt reads the ledger before its turn, listens on the bus during it and polls the ledger as a backstop; the run ends with the terminal `lifecycle.stopped` (reason, asker, partial answer), `App.Status` reports `stopped`, it is never retried, and its thread gets the partial answer plus the constant `runtime.StopMarker`. Once Stop returns nil the run ends stopped unless its turn had already returned its answer. Unknown, finished and foreign runs get the same answer and nothing is written for them.
- Compaction: `agentrt.Compaction{MaxInputTokens, KeepTurns, OnRequest}` (`fiber.WithCompaction`). With `OnRequest` on the agents and `runtime.WithCompactRequests` on the runtime, `runtime.Compact` (or `App.Compact`) publishes `control.compact` to the caller's tenant-keyed `agent:_control:compact-<key>`; the attempt running the turn compacts before its next model call. Live only, not recorded. Every compaction is published as opt-in `context.compacted` (`payload.Compaction`, trigger `requested` with `by` for a request).
- Usage: every model call is published as `usage.call` (fiber's attempt-unique AccountingID, saige's id beside it, agent, depth, model, requests, prompt/cached/cache-write/completion tokens, cost, context window) as it completes; a child run a host Delegator ran is reported once as `usage.child` (`runtime.ReportChildUsage(ctx, runID)`, which reads and checks the child in the ledger). The run's total (`payload.RunUsage{Own, Children, Total, Context}`) is on `lifecycle.completed`/`lifecycle.stopped`, `runtime.Output.Usage` (in the ledger) and `App.Status` (`Run.Usage`). Every call of every attempt that returned counts once: each attempt records its calls on the run (`event:mandatum.usage.a<N>#0`) before returning, a replay of the memoized agent adds nothing. Cost comes only from saige's price catalog, as int64 micro-units with currency and `as_of`, in the first priced call's currency with other currencies in `other_costs`; an unknown model reports tokens and no cost (`unpriced_calls`). Usage is opt-in for routes: only a route naming `usage` or one of its kinds receives it, and chat sinks never render it.
- Model fallbacks: `AgentSpec.Fallbacks []ModelRef{Provider, Model}` (JSON `fallbacks`), at most `agentspec.MaxFallbacks` (4), each a known provider and a model, none repeating the primary or another. `FallbackOn []string` (JSON `fallback_on`) narrows when a call falls through to named classes from `agentspec.FallbackConditions()` (`unavailable`, `rate_limit`, `transient`, `auth`, `context_length`, `content_filter`, or `any` alone, the default); it is a sorted set, requires fallbacks, and is ANDed with `fallback.DefaultFallbackOn` so terminal errors never fall through. `agentrt.New` builds every member through the provider table (one that cannot be built fails the build) and composes them with saige's `fallback.Of` under `fallback.DefaultFallbackOn`: outages, rate limits, auth and context-length errors fall through; cancellation, invalid requests and budget errors do not; a stream that already delivered output is not replayed. Order is hashed; an empty list hashes as before. Usage prices each call on the answering model's card, matched by the response's model name, and an unattributable call is unpriced.
- Parking on a person: a tool in a spec's `approvals` (or any saige `MarkedTool`) and the built-in `ask_person` tool (choice with `options`, or free-text reply) park the run on a typed `payload.Question{ID, Kind approval|choice|reply, Prompt, Options, Tool{Name, CallID, Arguments, Schema}, AskedOf, ExpiresAt, Default}`. The turn ends at the question before its batch of tool calls runs; the workflow body announces it once as a anchor step (`lifecycle.parked` with `Lifecycle.Question`), then waits on the write-once event record `event:mandatum.answer.<id>#0` and returns `run.ErrParked`, holding no worker. `runtime.Answer(ctx, AnswerRequest)` (`App.Answer`) validates the answer against the question, records it first-write-wins, and wakes the run (`runtime.WithWaker`); a second answer is told the first. The continuation (`mandatum.turn.resume`) rebuilds the parked conversation and answers its first model call with the recorded message, so saige runs the batch with the answer and every later request is byte-identical to an uninterrupted turn. Expiry (`runtime.WithQuestionTTL`, default 24h) records the default (deny for approvals) on the next poll; Stop resolves a parked question as stopped and the run ends `lifecycle.stopped` without resuming. `App.Status` reports `parked` with `Run.Question`. Per-call approval: a tool implementing `agentrt.Approving` (`Approval(saigetypes.ToolCallPart) (agentrt.ApprovalRequest{Prompt, AskedOf, Approvers, SelfApproval}, bool)`, decided from name and arguments) parks only the calls it asks about, through a saige ToolGate, as `approval` questions carrying `approvers`/`self_approval` (`payload.Question`), which replace the spec's approvers for that question; approved runs, denied or expired is refused, an unparkable turn refuses. Who may answer: an approval never by the requester (tag actor, bare or origin-qualified) or the credential that raised the run, unless the spec sets `self_approval`; `approvers` and `answerers` (principals or `role:<name>` via `runtime.WithRoles`) restrict approvals and choices/replies; refusals are `runtime.ErrNotAllowed`; `asked_of` is only a hint. `runtime.WithChildRuns` makes a delegation a child run the parent parks on (question kind `delegation`, answered by the child's ending); a blocking host Delegator holds a worker instead and can exhaust them (it can show a child's questions with `runtime.WatchChildQuestions`, `lifecycle.child.parked`). Repeated parks store the transcript once (`Parked.Since`); `runtime.WithRecordReader(durable.NewRecords(pool))` keeps polls off transcripts.
- Security boundaries: `pkg/signature` (HMAC over the raw body, verified before parsing, `hmac.Equal`, Slack replay window, fail closed) and the NGAC policy path (default deny, workspace areas and spawn allowlist).

## Key Files

- Leaves (stdlib only): pkg/topic/topic.go, pkg/address/address.go, pkg/envelope/envelope.go, pkg/signature/signature.go, pkg/agentspec/{agentspec,hash}.go
- Seams: pkg/connector/connector.go, pkg/bus/{bus,memory,redis,postgres,open}.go, pkg/bus/bustest/suite.go, pkg/registry/{registry,memory,postgres,specs,token}.go; conformance suites pkg/{registry/registrytest,knowledge/knowledgetest,thread/threadtest,toolprovider/toolprovidertest,blob/blobtest}
- Composition: pkg/agentrt/{agentrt,translate,citation,provider,spec,tools,usage,park}.go, pkg/agentrt/payload/payload.go, pkg/runtime/{runtime,sandbox,seq,stop,compact,usage,park}.go, pkg/router/{router,delivery}.go
- Connectors: pkg/connectors/{slack,github,jira,cron,webhook}/, shared helpers in pkg/connectors/internal/{httpjson,inbound,render,sink}/ and pkg/connectors/mention/
- Composition root: {fiber,app,config,extensions,connectors,knowledge,status}.go at the module root (`New` and its options for backends, model providers, tool sources, connectors and MCP tool providers), examples/downstream/main.go
- Example: examples/local/main.go (zero infrastructure, no API key, no network)

## API Cheatsheet

- Topics: `topic.Parse(s)`, `topic.All()`, `topic.Agent(name)`, `topic.Run(agent, runID)`, `t.Covers(other)`, `t.Name()`, `t.RunID()`
- Addresses: `address.Parse("github://urmzd/fiber/issues/42")`, `a.Connector`, `a.Workspace`, `a.Path`, `a.Param(k)`, `a.WithParam(k, v)`, `a.Resource()`
- Envelope: `envelope.Tag{ID, Tenant, Agent, Origin, Source, Text, Actor, Deliver, Meta, At}`, `tag.Validate()`, `tag.Routes()`; `envelope.Event{Seq, Topic, RunID, Tenant, Agent, Rev, Origin, Kind, Payload, At}`; `envelope.Route{Target, Kinds}.Wants(kind)`; `envelope.Filter{Kinds, Rev, Origin, RunID}.Allows(e)`; `envelope.Subscription{Topic, Filter, From}.Accepts(e)`
- Kinds: `delta.text`, `delta.thinking`, `delta.tool.call`, `delta.tool.done`, `delta.citation`, `lifecycle.{accepted,started,parked,resumed,completed,failed,stopped}`, `lifecycle.child.parked`, `action.taken`, `usage.{call,child}`, `context.compacted`, `control.{created,revised,deleted,stop,compact}`. `Kind.Family()` and `Kind.Matches(sel)` select a family or an exact kind.
- Connectors: `connector.Trigger{Ingest(ctx, out chan<- envelope.Tag)}`, `connector.Sink{Deliver(ctx, target, event)}`, `connector.Actor{Actions() []Action}`, `connector.RolesOf(c)`, `registry.Sink(target)`; sentinels `ErrUnsupported`, `ErrNotFound`, `ErrUndeliverable`
- Bus: `bus.Bus{Publish(ctx, e), Subscribe(ctx, sub) (Stream, error)}`, `Stream.Recv(ctx)`, `bustest.Run(t, factory)` holds any backend to the same contract
- Signature: `signature.NewSlack(secret)`, `signature.NewGitHub(secret)`, `Verify(header, body)`; sentinels `ErrSignatureMismatch`, `ErrTimestampSkew`, `ErrMalformed`, `ErrNoSecret`; `DefaultWindow` is 5 minutes and the boundary is inclusive
- Payloads: `payload.Of(event)` returns the typed body; `payload.Decode[T](event)`; types `Text`, `Thinking`, `ToolCall{ID, Name, Phase, Arguments, ArgumentsBytes}`, `ToolDone{ID, Name, Result, Error, Arguments, ArgumentsBytes}` (arguments as compact JSON, left out whole above `payload.MaxToolArguments` (8 KiB) with their size in `ArgumentsBytes`, scrubbed first by `agentrt.WithToolArguments`), `Citation{Label, Text, Source, Index}`, `Lifecycle{Attempt, Rev, Terminal, Question, Answer}`, `Question`, `Answer{QuestionID, Decision, Arguments, Choice, Text, Note, By, At, Expired}`, `ChildQuestion{RunID, Agent, Question}`, `Stopped{Attempt, Rev, Reason, By, Text}`, `StopRequest{RunID, Reason, By}`, `Compaction{Trigger, By, Strategy, TokensBefore, TokensAfter, Summarized, Kept}`, `CompactRequest{RunID, By, At}`, `Action`, `UsageCall{AccountingID, Agent, Depth, Model, Requests, PromptTokens, CachedPromptTokens, CacheWriteTokens, CompletionTokens, ResponseCacheHit, Cost, ContextWindow}`, `UsageChild{AccountingID, RunID, Agent, Depth, Usage}`, `RunUsage{Own, Children, Total, Context}`, `Usage{..., Cost, OtherCosts, UnpricedCalls}`, `Cost{Micros, Currency, AsOf}`; `payload.Tally` counts each AccountingID once
- App: `fiber.New(ctx, fiber.WithTenant(t), fiber.WithPostgres(pool), fiber.WithBus(b), ...)`, `app.Run(ctx)` / `RunDelivery` / `RunExecution`, `app.Close()`, `app.Invoke(ctx, tag) (runtime.Acceptance, error)`, `app.Status(ctx, tenant, runID) (fiber.Run, error)`, `app.Stop`, `app.Compact`, `app.Answer`, `app.Index(ctx, tenant, source, paths...)`, `app.Webhooks()`, `app.WebhookHandler()`, accessors `Registry`, `Bus`, `Runtime`, `Router`, `Connectors`, `Knowledge`, `Threads`, `ToolProviders`, `Blobs`; backends are constructed: `bus.NewMemory()`, `bus.NewRedis(client)` (size it with `bus.RedisPoolSize`), `bus.NewPostgres(pool)`
